class.name: PhysXVehicle3D
class.brief_description: A PhysX-specific 4-wheel vehicle, powered by PxVehicle2 -- an alternative to the stock, backend-agnostic [VehicleBody3D], not a replacement for it.
class.description: [VehicleBody3D]/[VehicleWheel3D] work on this module already (no PhysX-specific code needed) and stay the right choice for a project that wants to swap physics backends freely. [PhysXVehicle3D] exists for real PxVehicle2 capability that backend-agnostic model structurally can't offer: a real engine torque response, Ackermann steering correction (inner/outer front wheels turn by different angles in a turn), and a real slip-based tire friction curve (grip peaks at a small amount of wheel slip and falls off once the tire is fully sliding/locked, instead of one flat friction number). Node structure mirrors [VehicleBody3D]/[VehicleWheel3D] on purpose: add a [CollisionShape3D] child with a [BoxShape3D] for the chassis, and exactly 4 [PhysXVehicleWheel3D] children for the wheels -- exactly 2 of them need [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.use_as_steering] enabled (the front axle). Each wheel's own [member Node3D.position] is where it rests under static load (the same convention [VehicleWheel3D] uses), so a [MeshInstance3D] parented under a wheel tracks the real, live suspension/steering motion automatically, and already sits at the right height in the editor before Play. Drive it every physics tick by setting [member throttle], [member brake], [member steer], and (once actually stopped) [member reverse] -- these use PxVehicleCommandState's own convention ([member throttle]/[member brake] in [code][0, 1][/code], [member steer] in [code][-1, 1][/code]), not [VehicleBody3D]'s raw force/angle convention. Only runs in an actual running game, never in the editor -- placing or moving the node in the Inspector does not simulate or fall under gravity.

method.name: add_collision_exception_with
method.description: Stops the car and [param body] (a [PhysicsBody3D] or another PhysX vehicle) colliding: they pass through each other, its wheels included, as with [method PhysicsBody3D.add_collision_exception_with]. Either side having the exception is enough, so a [RigidBody3D] or [CharacterBody3D] needs nothing of its own.

method.name: apply_central_force
method.description: Applies a world-space force at the chassis's center of mass for this physics step (call it every step to keep pushing), as [method RigidBody3D.apply_central_force]. For autopilot steering and docking assists, wind, gravity wells.

method.name: apply_central_impulse
method.description: Applies a one-off world-space impulse at the center of mass, as [method RigidBody3D.apply_central_impulse]: the velocity changes by [param impulse] / [member mass] at once.

method.name: apply_force
method.description: Applies a world-space force at [param position] for this physics step, as [method RigidBody3D.apply_force]: [param position] is an offset from the car's origin, in world axes. Off the center of mass it also turns the car.

method.name: apply_impulse
method.description: Applies a one-off world-space impulse at [param position] (an offset from the car's origin, in world axes), as [method RigidBody3D.apply_impulse].

method.name: apply_torque
method.description: Applies a world-space torque for this physics step, as [method RigidBody3D.apply_torque].

method.name: apply_torque_impulse
method.description: Applies a one-off world-space angular impulse, as [method RigidBody3D.apply_torque_impulse].

method.name: get_actor_position
method.description: The real PhysX actor's own world-space origin -- for comparing against this node's own [member Node3D.global_position] (which tracks the same point) when diagnosing a suspension/placement issue.

method.name: get_angular_velocity
method.description: The chassis's world-space angular velocity, in radians per second.

method.name: get_collision_exceptions
method.description: The bodies and vehicles this car has collision exceptions with.

method.name: get_current_gear
method.description: The gear engaged now, numbered as [member gear]: -1 reverse, 0 neutral, 1 and up forward. It reads 0 while a shift is under way. With [constant DRIVETRAIN_DIRECT], 1, or -1 with [member reverse].

method.name: get_engine_rpm
method.description: The engine speed in revolutions per minute. 0 with [constant DRIVETRAIN_DIRECT].

method.name: get_forward
method.description: Current world-space forward direction of the chassis: its local +Z axis, the same forward as [VehicleBody3D] ([constant Vector3.MODEL_FRONT]).

method.name: get_forward_speed
method.description: Current speed along the car's own forward axis, in m/s. Positive while driving forward, negative while rolling backward -- a simple way to decide when it is safe to switch [member reverse] on (a real gear should only engage once the car has actually stopped, not while still coasting forward).

method.name: get_linear_velocity
method.description: The chassis's world-space linear velocity. It reads the chassis itself, so a velocity just set with [method set_linear_velocity] or changed by an impulse reads back at once.

method.name: get_rid
method.description: The car's identity in the physics server: a raycast or shape query that hits it, or a [CharacterBody3D] that bumps into it, reports this RID as the collider's (and the car node as the collider). Put it in a query's [code]exclude[/code] list to see past the car, or pass it to [method PhysicsServer3D.body_add_collision_exception] to make a body ignore it. It stands for the car only: setting its state through [PhysicsServer3D] doesn't move the car.

method.name: get_target_gear
method.description: The gear the gearbox is shifting to, numbered as [member gear] (the current gear when no shift is under way). A new gear is taken only once the current shift has finished ([member gear_switch_time]).

method.name: get_wheel_jounce
method.description: How compressed wheel [param wheel]'s suspension is right now, from [code]0[/code] (fully extended / max droop) to that wheel's own [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.suspension_travel] (fully compressed / bottomed out). [param wheel] is the child index among this node's [PhysXVehicleWheel3D] children, in the order they were added -- not a fixed front-left/front-right/rear-left/rear-right order. Useful for tuning [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.suspension_stiffness]: resting jounce well under half of [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.suspension_travel] leaves real margin before the suspension bottoms out under braking, cornering, or a bump.

method.name: get_wheel_separation
method.description: [code]0[/code] when wheel [param wheel] can reach the ground within its suspension travel. A negative value means the wheel is penetrating the ground even at full compression -- [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.suspension_travel] is too short for the current ride height. [param wheel] uses the same child-index convention as [method get_wheel_jounce].

method.name: is_sleeping
method.description: Returns whether the underlying PhysX vehicle actor is currently sleeping.

method.name: remove_collision_exception_with
method.description: Removes an exception added with [method add_collision_exception_with].

method.name: set_angular_velocity
method.description: Sets the chassis's world-space angular velocity (radians per second) directly.

method.name: set_linear_velocity
method.description: Sets the chassis's world-space linear velocity directly. [method get_linear_velocity] reads it back at once.

method.name: teleport
method.description: Moves the car to [param transform] at once, without rebuilding it (the same chassis, wheels and settings carry on). Unless [param keep_velocity] is [code]true[/code], it arrives at rest, its wheels no longer spinning. Moving the node itself doesn't move a car that is simulating: its transform follows the chassis.

members.member: How much Ackermann steering correction to apply to the front (steering) axle, from [code]0[/code] (both front wheels always turn by the same angle, like [VehicleWheel3D]) to [code]1[/code] (full correction: the inside wheel of a turn steers more sharply than the outside wheel, matching how a real front axle is geometrically linked).
The automatic gearbox shifts down when the engine falls below this fraction of [member engine_max_rpm]. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].
The least time, in seconds, between two shifts the automatic gearbox makes. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].
The automatic gearbox shifts up when the engine passes this fraction of [member engine_max_rpm]. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].

A control, read every physics tick. If [code]true[/code], the automatic gearbox picks the forward gears. While [member clutch] is pressed past halfway it holds its gear, so revving against the clutch for a launch doesn't shift up standing still. If [code]false[/code], the gearbox goes to [member gear]. Either way, [member reverse] selects the reverse gear. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].

Brake pedal input, [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code]. Scales up to [member max_brake_torque] of braking torque at each wheel. Set every physics tick from script; does not persist on its own the way a real pedal would.

Whether the vehicle is allowed to sleep after remaining below the PhysX space's configured sleep thresholds. The global [code]physics/physx_3d/simulation/allow_sleep[/code] project setting can disable sleeping for all PhysX bodies.

The vehicle center of mass in the vehicle's local coordinates when [member center_of_mass_mode] is [code]Custom[/code]. Lowering the Y coordinate can make the vehicle more resistant to rollover. In [code]Auto[/code] mode, the center of mass follows the chassis [CollisionShape3D] child position.
Whether to derive the center of mass from the chassis [CollisionShape3D] position ([code]Auto[/code]) or use [member center_of_mass] directly ([code]Custom[/code]).
A control, read every physics tick: 0 engaged, 1 fully pressed (the engine turns freely of the wheels). Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].

A control, read every physics tick. If [code]true[/code], a manual gearbox changes gear as soon as [member gear] (or [member reverse]) asks, disconnecting the engine for the shift by itself. If [code]false[/code], it changes gear only while [member clutch] is pressed past halfway, and otherwise stays in the gear it has. The automatic gearbox ignores it. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].

How strongly the engaged clutch couples the engine to the wheels. A weak clutch slips longer before the engine and wheels match speed. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].

Same meaning as [member CollisionObject3D.collision_layer]. Applies to the chassis only -- the wheels do not have their own collision shapes (their ground contact is handled entirely by the suspension, not by a physical wheel shape touching the road).

Same meaning as [member CollisionObject3D.collision_mask]. Applies to the chassis (see [member collision_layer]) and to the wheels' ground raycasts: like a [RayCast3D], a wheel only rests on a shape whose collision layer is in this mask, and never on an [Area3D].
How the engine's torque is shared between the wheels with [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.use_as_traction]. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].

How [member throttle] reaches the wheels. [constant DRIVETRAIN_DIRECT] is wheel torque up to [member max_engine_torque]. [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE] is PhysX's engine drive: an engine, clutch, gearbox and differential, set up with the engine, gearbox and differential properties, which the inspector shows only in that mode. Changing it while playing rebuilds the vehicle.

How quickly the engine slows on its own at full throttle. The damping eases between this and the zero-throttle rates as the throttle moves. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].
How quickly the engine slows on its own with no throttle and the clutch pressed. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].
How quickly the engine slows on its own with no throttle and the clutch engaged (engine braking). Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].
The engine's idle speed, in revolutions per minute. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].
The engine's top speed, in revolutions per minute: it can't rev past it. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].
The engine's rotational inertia. Lower revs up and down faster. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].
The engine's torque at the top of [member engine_torque_curve], in newton-meters, before the gearing multiplies it. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].

The engine's torque (as a fraction of [member engine_peak_torque]) against its speed (as a fraction of [member engine_max_rpm]): the curve's domain is mapped to 0..1 of the engine speed. PhysX takes 8 points; a curve with more is sampled at 8 even speeds. If [code]null[/code], the torque is flat. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].
The ratio applied after every gear, between the gearbox and the wheels. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].

Anti-roll bar stiffness connecting the front-left and front-right wheels. A positive value is a real anti-roll bar: it resists the difference in suspension compression between the two wheels, reducing body roll during cornering. A negative value does the opposite -- it amplifies that difference, exaggerating roll instead of resisting it, which is a cheaper and more targeted way to get a more dramatic cornering lean than lowering [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.suspension_stiffness] further (that also softens straight-line bump absorption; this only affects side-to-side compression difference). [code]0[/code] disables the bar entirely.

A control, read every physics tick when [member automatic_transmission] is [code]false[/code]: the gear the gearbox goes to. -1 is reverse, 0 neutral, 1 first gear, up to the number of [member gear_ratios]. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].
The forward gears' ratios, first gear to top. They must be positive and descending. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].
How long a shift takes, in seconds. The engine is disconnected from the wheels meanwhile. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].
Brake input for the rear wheels only, from [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code], on top of [member brake] (up to [member max_brake_torque]): a parking brake, or to lock the rear wheels into a slide.

With [constant DIFFERENTIAL_LIMITED_SLIP] and both axles driven: the largest ratio between the front and rear wheels' speeds before torque moves to the slower axle. 0 leaves it open; otherwise it must be greater than [member limited_slip_center_target].
With [constant DIFFERENTIAL_LIMITED_SLIP]: the speed ratio between the axles that moving torque aims for once [member limited_slip_center_bias] is passed. Between 1 and the bias.

With [constant DIFFERENTIAL_LIMITED_SLIP] and both front wheels driven: the largest ratio between their speeds before torque moves to the slower wheel. 0 leaves the front axle open; otherwise it must be greater than [member limited_slip_front_target].
With [constant DIFFERENTIAL_LIMITED_SLIP]: the front wheels' speed ratio that moving torque aims for once [member limited_slip_front_bias] is passed. Between 1 and the bias.
With [constant DIFFERENTIAL_LIMITED_SLIP]: how quickly a wheel speed ratio is brought to its target.

With [constant DIFFERENTIAL_LIMITED_SLIP] and both rear wheels driven: the largest ratio between their speeds before torque moves to the slower wheel. 0 leaves the rear axle open; otherwise it must be greater than [member limited_slip_rear_target].
With [constant DIFFERENTIAL_LIMITED_SLIP]: the rear wheels' speed ratio that moving torque aims for once [member limited_slip_rear_bias] is passed. Between 1 and the bias.
Total mass of the vehicle, in kg.

The braking torque applied to each wheel when [member brake] is [code]1[/code]. Higher values stop the wheel's own rotation faster, but do not by themselves determine whether the tire skids once locked -- see [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.tire_friction] for that.

The drive torque applied to every wheel with [member PhysXVehicleWheel3D.use_as_traction] enabled when [member throttle] is [code]1[/code] (a real direct-drive response, unlike [member VehicleBody3D.engine_force] which is a raw force value with no torque curve). Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_DIRECT]; the engine drive uses [member engine_peak_torque] and the gearing instead.
The steering angle, in radians, applied to the front axle when [member steer] is [code]1[/code] or [code]-1[/code]. The default (~34°) is a realistic maximum for a real car's front wheels.

The vehicle's own rotational inertia around its X/Y/Z axes. Higher values resist rotation (pitch/yaw/roll) more -- tune the Y (yaw) component if the car turns too eagerly or too sluggishly for its size.

The contact material of the chassis box: what the vehicle feels like when its body, not its wheels, touches something -- on its roof or side after a flip, grinding along a wall, bottoming out. [member PhysicsMaterial.friction], [member PhysicsMaterial.rough], [member PhysicsMaterial.bounce] and [member PhysicsMaterial.absorbent] combine with the other side the same way as for any [RigidBody3D] on this module. If [code]null[/code], the chassis uses friction [code]0.5[/code] and bounce [code]0.1[/code]; lower the friction for a body that skids further after a flip. Changes (including edits to the assigned material) apply immediately, without rebuilding the vehicle. Tire grip is not affected; it comes from the wheels' tire settings.

Same as [member front_anti_roll_stiffness], connecting the rear-left and rear-right wheels instead. Tuning front and rear independently changes handling balance: a stiffer (more positive) front bar relative to the rear tends toward understeer, and vice versa for oversteer -- same real-world relationship a physical anti-roll bar has.

Switches the drivetrain's gear between forward and reverse -- a real gear change (PxVehicle2 has no neutral-coast/instant-reverse shortcut), so [member throttle] in reverse gear still needs to first bring the car to a stop if it was moving forward, same as a real car. Check [method get_forward_speed] before engaging this from a driving script.
The reverse gear's ratio, as a positive number. Only with [member drivetrain] set to [constant DRIVETRAIN_ENGINE].
Steering input, [code]-1[/code] to [code]1[/code]. Scales up to [member max_steer_angle] on the front (steering) axle, modified by [member ackermann_strength]. Set every physics tick from script.

Throttle input, [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code]. Scales up to [member max_engine_torque] of drive torque at each traction wheel, in whichever direction [member reverse] currently selects. Set every physics tick from script.

Where the tire forces push on the chassis, from [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code]. At [code]0[/code] (PhysX's own default) they act at the suspension mount, usually above the center of mass, so the body barely pitches or rolls under them. At [code]1[/code] they act at the tire's contact patch on the ground, like [VehicleWheel3D]'s: hard acceleration squats the rear and can lift the front wheels (a wheelie, with a high, rear-set [member center_of_mass] and grippy driven tires), and braking dives the nose. In between, the point moves down by that fraction of the way. Cornering forces get the same lever, so a grippy car with a high center of mass can roll over in a hard turn; less front grip than rear, a lower center of mass or stiffer anti-roll bars keep it on its wheels. Changing it while playing rebuilds the vehicle.

A live multiplier on every tire's grip: below [code]1[/code] for ice, mud or wet roads, above for sticky tires. It takes effect at once, without rebuilding the vehicle (the wheels' own [code]tire_*[/code] properties rebuild it), so it can follow the ground the vehicle is on every frame.

constants.constant: The center of mass is the position of the chassis [CollisionShape3D] child.
The center of mass is [member center_of_mass].
The engine's torque is split evenly between the traction wheels, whatever each one does: a wheel on ice spins and the others get no more.
PhysX's four-wheel-drive differential: torque moves away from a wheel spinning faster than its partner on the same axle, or from the faster axle, past the [code]limited_slip_*[/code] biases.
Throttle is wheel torque, up to [member max_engine_torque], forward or in reverse.
PhysX's engine drive: an engine with a torque curve drives the traction wheels through a clutch, a gearbox (automatic or manual) and a differential.
